group_secondaryOfLabel: This site is a secondary of
group_tenantWarning: This site uses wildcard tenant subdomains. A grouped subdomain is carved out of that space and routed to the secondary instead.
group_noSecondariesLabel: No secondaries yet. Add a site below to put it on a subdomain of
group_sharedDbTitleOn: Sharing the main database (click for separate)
group_sharedDbTitleOff: Separate database (click to share the main)
group_shareDbCheckbox: Share {name}'s database instead of a separate one
group_putOnSubdomain: Put {domain} on a subdomain of another site.
dashboard_subtitle: Everything servlo is running, at a glance
onboarding_subtitle: Your local PHP development manager. Get started in three steps.
onboarding_park_body: All projects under a parked directory get auto-linked as you create them.
onboarding_link_body: Already have a Laravel, Symfony, or WordPress site somewhere? Link it directly.
onboarding_service_body: Spin up MySQL, Redis, Meilisearch, and more from the bundled presets.
onboarding_dismissHint: Dismiss this card to hide it permanently
onboarding_adminOnly: Only an admin can do this.
dashboard_hero_allGood: Everything's running smoothly · {sitesRunning}/{sitesTotal} sites · {servicesActive} services active
dashboard_hero_coreDownHint: Core services are required for sites to respond.
dashboard_hero_updatesMixed: Servlo v{servlo} and {count} service update(s) available
dashboard_workers_empty: No queue, schedule, or framework workers configured.
dashboard_activity_empty: No activity yet, events will appear here as things change.
services_checkUpdatesTitle: Force a fresh registry lookup, bypassing the cache
services_upgradeWarning: Upgrade to {tag} (may require manual data migration, review the service docs first)
services_migrateExplain: Migrate to {tag} via dump+restore (safer than Upgrade for data-incompatible jumps)
services_rollbackExplain: Roll back to {tag} (the image running before the last update)
sites_reqstats_allGood: No slow routes, everything is within the typical range
sites_reqstats_profileHint: Profiling every request. Reload a slow route, then read its flame graph in the Profiler.
sites_timing_coldHint: Cold start (first request after the site went idle), excluded from timing
sites_pausedDetail_hint: Nginx is not serving {domain} while it's paused. Resume to bring it back online.
sites_unlinkBody: The site stops being served by nginx. Its files stay on disk and you can link it again at any time.
sites_controls_httpsUnavailable: HTTPS unavailable, servlo is not managing DNS
sites_controls_queueToggle_failing: Queue worker is failing, click to restart
sites_controls_horizonToggle_failing: Horizon is failing, click to restart
sites_controls_horizonReloadToggle_on: Auto-reload on file changes is on, click to turn off
sites_controls_horizonReloadToggle_off: Auto-reload on file changes is off, click to turn on (horizon:listen)
horizonWatcher_body: Horizon auto-reload watches your files with chokidar, which isn't installed in this project. Vite 8 no longer ships it, so servlo can add it as a dev dependency.
sites_controls_octaneRunning: Octane is running in FrankenPHP worker mode
sites_controls_octaneReloadToggle_on: Auto-reload on file changes is on, click to turn off
sites_controls_octaneReloadToggle_off: Auto-reload on file changes is off, click to turn on (octane:start --watch)
octaneWatcher_body: Octane auto-reload watches your files with chokidar, which isn't installed in this project. Vite 8 no longer ships it, so servlo can add it as a dev dependency.
sites_controls_stripePathHint: The route Stripe events forward to on your app, e.g. /stripe/webhook for Laravel or your own route for any other framework.
sites_appLogs_noFiles: No log files in storage/logs yet. They'll appear here as soon as the app writes one.
sites_appLogs_clearTitle: Delete log files to reclaim disk (the active log is recreated automatically)
sites_appLogs_clearModalBody: This permanently deletes every log file in this site's storage/logs to reclaim {size}. The active log is recreated automatically on the app's next write.
services_env_connectHint: Use {loopback4} or {loopback6} from your host. Inside containers use the hostname shown in the .env block below.
services_env_none: This service has no env vars.
services_banner_description: {description}. Installs as a custom service that auto-starts {svcName}.
services_banner_dismiss: Dismiss, you can still add this from the Services + button
services_preset_subtitle: Bundled, opt-in services. Installing one adds it as a custom service so you can start, stop, or remove it from the Services tab.
services_install_offer: {name} is listed for this site but isn't installed yet.
services_install_custom: {name} is a custom service with no bundled preset. Define it in ~/.config/servlo/services/{name}.yaml, then link the site again.
system_nginx_confHint: Global http-level overrides (gzip, proxy buffers, client_max_body_size…). Servlo never overwrites this file; saving reloads nginx.
system_dns_degradedHint: servlo-dns is healthy and answering directly, but the system resolver isn't routing your domains to it, usually because a VPN client rewrote DNS. Sites still resolve, and servlo re-syncs container DNS automatically when the VPN connection changes.
system_dns_fixHint: Try {start}, or run {cmd} to fix DNS.
system_dns_upstream_desc: servlo-dns forwards queries outside your local TLD to these servers. One per line; an optional #port suffix is allowed (e.g. 192.168.100.129#5353). Leave empty to auto-detect from the system resolver.
system_dns_upstream_saved: Saved. servlo-dns was restarted with the new upstream.
system_watcher_description: Monitors parked directories, site files, and DNS health. Logs WARN and ERROR events by default; set {env} in the service environment for verbose output.
system_watcher_quiet: No events yet, watcher is running quietly.
system_php_iniHint: Overrides for memory_limit, opcache, realpath_cache, etc. Servlo never overwrites this file; saving restarts PHP.
system_php_stopWarn: {count} site(s) use this version, they will stop working
system_php_addHint: Pick a version to build and install. The first build can take a few minutes.
system_php_allInstalled: All supported PHP versions are already installed.
system_php_baseUpdateHint: The prebuilt base image was refreshed upstream. Rebuild to pick it up.
system_php_rebuildHint: Rebuild this version's image from the current base
system_php_checkUpdatesTitle: Ask the registry whether the base image has been refreshed
system_php_checkUpdatesFound: A refreshed base image is available
notify_php_base_update_body: A refreshed base image is published. Rebuild to pick it up.
notify_tool_update_body: Version {version} is pinned. Apply it from the Tools card.
system_php_removeConfirmBody: This stops and removes the PHP-FPM service and container for this version. The build cache is kept, so you can reinstall it later.
system_node_managedBySystemHint: To install or change Node.js versions from here, run `servlo install` in a terminal and accept servlo-managed Node.
system_node_usingBunHint: Node isn't managed by servlo and bun is installed, so JS tooling (Vite, installs, builds) runs through bun.
system_node_manageHint: Installs node/npm/npx shims and a default version via the selected version manager.
system_node_unmanageHint: Removes servlo's node shims (and, with fnm, the versions it installed) for a clean system (use bun or your own Node).
system_node_managerFnm: Use fnm, the version manager servlo bundles.
system_node_managerNvm: Use your own installed nvm instead of fnm.
system_node_managerNvmMissing: nvm is not installed on this machine.
system_node_cannotRemove: Cannot remove, sites are using this version
system_node_cannotRemoveSystem: Node is managed by the system
system_node_installNewHint: Enter a major version (e.g. {major}) or a specific one (e.g. {specific}). Installed via fnm.
system_servlo_updateHint: Servlo updates by re-running its installer, which needs an interactive terminal so it can prompt for sudo and show the download progress. Run {cmd} in an SSH session on this server.
system_tools_description: Standalone binaries servlo installs and manages: Composer and fnm.
system_tools_checkTitle: Ask GitHub whether newer versions have been pinned
system_tools_checkUpToDate: Every tool is at its pinned version
system_workerMode_description: Controls how framework workers (queue, schedule, horizon, reverb, custom) are launched on macOS. The default is exec mode for lower memory.
system_workerMode_exec_description: One podman exec per worker into the shared FPM container, supervised by systemd with a pid-file dedup guard. Near-zero memory overhead per worker. Matches the Linux profile.
system_workerMode_container_description: One detached container per worker, spawned from the FPM image. Higher memory (especially for Horizon which supervises its own pool), but 1:1 supervisor boundary with podman's own restart policy.
system_workerMode_note_body: Changing the mode stops every active worker in its old shape, cleans up the on-disk artifacts, and restarts it in the new shape. Other servlo services (FPM, nginx, DNS, built-in services) aren't touched.
system_workerMode_confirm_body: Switch from {from} to {to}? Every active worker will be stopped, its on-disk artifacts cleaned up, and restarted in the new shape.
system_workerMode_confirm_hint: FPM, nginx, DNS, and built-in services are not touched. This may take a few seconds.
system_workerMode_apply_failed: Could not switch worker runtime. Workers were not changed.
system_autostart_description: When enabled, servlo-panel and servlo-watcher start automatically on every login.
system_lan_exposedDescription: Sites are reachable from other devices on the LAN at {ip}. Managed database, cache, and mail access is controlled separately below.
system_lan_loopbackDescription: Servlo is bound to loopback only ({loop4} and {loop6} on dual-stack hosts), invisible to other devices on the network. Safe for untrusted wifi (cafés, conference networks). Expose to share your sites with another machine on a trusted LAN.
system_lan_macosWarning: macOS: This toggle controls DNS resolution ({pattern} → 127.0.0.1 or LAN IP). Ports 80 and 443 are always reachable from the LAN due to a gvproxy limitation. Managed service ports remain restricted unless explicitly enabled with the separate control below.
system_lan_progress_doneExposed: Servlo is now exposed on the LAN at {ip}.
system_lan_progress_doneHidden: Servlo is back on loopback only.
system_remote_description: When disabled, only loopback ({loop4} and {loop6}) can reach the dashboard. Enable to grant LAN clients access with HTTP Basic auth. Loopback always bypasses authentication, so you can never lock yourself out from this machine.
system_remote_inertWarning: Credentials are stored but inert, LAN exposure is off, so LAN clients still get 403. Run {cmd} (or click {btn} above) to make them active.
system_remote_enableDisabledHint: Run lan:expose first, without it the dashboard is loopback-only and credentials would be inert.
system_remote_exposeFirst: Expose servlo to the LAN first. Dashboard credentials are only meaningful while the dashboard is reachable from other devices.
system_remoteModal_title: Enable LAN access to the dashboard
system_remoteModal_subtitle: Set a username and password. LAN clients will need to present them via HTTP Basic auth to reach the dashboard. Loopback access from this machine always bypasses the gate, so you can never lock yourself out.
system_language_description: The interface language. Defaults to your browser language; falls back to English.
apps_empty: No service dashboards are active. Start a service with a dashboard (e.g. rustfs, phpMyAdmin) to see it here.
link_envWarning: The site is linked, but its environment setup did not finish.
queries_description: Captures every database query with its SQL, bindings, duration, and the line that ran it.
queries_disabled_body: Enable it to record every database query with its SQL, bindings, duration, and the line that ran it.
queries_waiting_body: Run a request or an artisan command and the queries will appear here.
sites_nginx_desc: Included at the end of this site’s server block. Servlo never overwrites this file; saving reloads nginx.
nginxEditor_resetBody: Delete the saved nginx override for {domain} and reload nginx? The bundled defaults will apply. Backups are kept and can be restored later.
nginxEditor_confirmBody: Save these changes to {domain}'s nginx override and reload nginx?
nginxEditor_backupLabel: Back up the current file first
nginxEditor_restoreBody: Replace the current override for {domain} with {name}. The backup will be removed after the restore completes.
nginxEditor_restoreNoDiff: The backup matches the current file line for line.
notify_toggle_on: Notifications are on, click to disable
notify_toggle_off: Notifications are off, click to enable
notify_toggle_blocked: Notifications are blocked by the browser
envEditor_backupLabel: Back up the current file first
envEditor_restoreBody: Replace the current {file} with {name}. The backup will be removed after the restore completes.
envEditor_restoreNoDiff: The backup matches the current file line for line.
envEditor_proposeFailed: Could not load the missing keys
envEditor_proposeModalBody: Pick which keys to add to {file}. Values are copied from .env.example, so review them and fill in real ones after adding.
services_tuning_desc: Loaded after the bundled config, so your values win. Servlo never overwrites this file; saving restarts the service.
tuningEditor_confirmBody: Save these changes to {name}'s config and restart the service?
tuningEditor_backupLabel: Back up the current file first
tuningEditor_restoreBody: Replace {name}'s saved config with {backup} and restart the service. The backup is removed after the restart completes.
tuningEditor_restoreNoDiff: The backup matches the current file line for line.
tuningEditor_resetBody: Reset {name}'s saved config to bundled defaults and restart the service? The current content is staged as a recovery backup you can restore from later.
tuningEditor_rolledBack: The service didn't restart cleanly, so your previous config was restored and is running again.
tuningEditor_resetRolledBack: The service didn't restart cleanly, so your previous config was restored (kept as {name}) and is running again.
services_portConflictTitle: Port {ports} already in use on the host. Stop the conflicting process or change the servlo port. Run `servlo doctor` for the find command on your OS.
services_ports_publishedHelp: Moves the host port {name} is published on. Containerized apps reach it by name and are unaffected; update host clients to the new port.
services_ports_extraHelp: Additional host:container mappings published alongside the main port.
services_ports_extraPresetOnly: Extra ports are available for built-in services only.
system_php_ports_help: Extra host ports published on PHP {version}'s FPM container, so a process you run in the container (a Vite dev server, a websocket, an ad-hoc listener) is reachable at localhost:PORT. If a host port is already taken, servlo moves it to the next free one. Changing this restarts PHP {version} for every site on it.
services_reinstall_body: Stops, removes, and reinstalls {name} at the current version. Use this when a service update produced data incompatible with the new image.
services_reinstall_resetHint: Renames the data dir aside (recoverable as {name}.pre-remove-<ts>) and recreates databases or buckets for {count} linked site(s) on the fresh service.
services_reinstall_wipeWarn: Data will be wiped. The reinstall will recreate empty databases or buckets for the linked site(s), but their previous content is gone (the rename-aside copy can be restored manually).
services_reinstall_menuTitle: Stop, remove, and reinstall at the current version. Optional reset-data wipes the data dir and reprovisions linked sites.
services_delete_breakWarn: Removing it will break those sites until you reinstall.
services_delete_body: Stops the unit, removes the container, and deletes the service config. Default services can be reinstalled later from the preset list.
notify_banner_subtitle: Skip checking the dashboard. servlo will pop a notification for worker failures, service updates and finished operations.
notify_settings_master_hint: Master switch. Turns every category off when disabled.
notify_settings_category_worker_failed_h: Queue, Horizon, Reverb, schedule or stripe worker enters a failed state.
notify_settings_category_op_done_hint: Long-running install / migrate / reinstall / update completed (or failed).
notify_settings_category_update_availabl: Registry has a newer image tag for a running service.
notify_settings_category_nplusone_hint: A request or worker ran the same query shape repeatedly. Warns once per route.
notify_settings_category_slow_route_hint: A route is running well above the site's typical response time. Warns once per route.
notify_settings_category_dump_hint: ray() / dump() / var-dump packet arrived from a site. Off by default, typically noisy.
notify_settings_devices_none: No browser subscribed for push notifications yet.
notify_settings_denied_body: You picked Block when this page asked for permission. Browsers won't ever ask again automatically, so this site has to be unblocked by hand.
notify_settings_denied_chromium: Click the small icon at the left of the address bar, open Site settings, then set Notifications to Allow.
notify_settings_denied_firefox: Click the small icon at the left of the address bar, find Notifications under Permissions, and remove the Block.
notify_settings_denied_safari: Open Safari, then Settings, Websites, Notifications. Find this site and switch it to Allow.
notify_settings_denied_generic: Open this browser's site-permission settings for the page and switch Notifications to Allow.
notify_settings_denied_still_blocked: Still blocked. If you just changed the permission, reload this page.
notify_settings_unsubscribed_body: Open tabs will still pop notifications, but servlo won't push anything when the tab is closed.
notify_test_body: If you see this, push notifications are working.
nginxGlobalEditor_confirmBody: Save these changes to the global nginx http override and reload nginx?
nginxGlobalEditor_resetBody: Delete the saved global nginx http override and reload nginx? The bundled defaults will apply. Backups are kept and can be restored later.
nginxGlobalEditor_restoreBody: Replace the current global http override with {name}. The backup will be removed after the restore completes.
services_dash_noInstalled: No services installed yet. Add one below to get started.
dbconn_desc: Where sites keep their data. A connection is either a database service running here or a managed database somewhere else.
dbconn_removeBody: This forgets how servlo reaches this database. Nothing on the database server itself is deleted.
dbconn_noServices: No database service is installed here yet.
dbconn_managedNote: Servlo opens the connection before it saves it, and creates each site's database and its own user on the managed server when that site is set up.
dbconn_passwordHint: Kept on the server and never read back into the panel.
dbconn_caCertHint: The .crt your provider gives you, for verify-ca. Servlo keeps its own copy.
dbconn_site_desc: Which connection this site's database lives on.
dbconn_site_hint: This changes where the site's next servlo env writes. It does not move any data.
dbuser_desc: The account this site reaches its database as. Its grants stop at this site's own schemas, so one site cannot read another's data.
dbuser_adminFallbackHint: This site was created before per-site accounts. Run servlo env in it, or rotate below, to give it one of its own.
dbuser_rotateHint: Issues a new password, updates it on the database server and writes it into {keys}. The application picks it up at its next deploy or PHP-FPM reload.
dbuser_rotateHintNoKeys: Issues a new password and updates it on the database server.
dbuser_rotated: Rotated. {keys} updated; the application picks the new password up at its next deploy or PHP-FPM reload.
dbuser_confirmBody: The new password is written into the site's env file. Until the application is redeployed or PHP-FPM reloads, it keeps serving on the connection it already has open.
services_tools_hint: Expose this service’s client tools on your host so you can run them against an external database or from an IDE like PhpStorm.
services_tools_shadow: You already have this installed; enabling the shim shadows it on your PATH.
services_tools_none: This service exposes no client tools.
workspaces_deleteBody: The workspace is removed. Its sites stay linked and become ungrouped.
dashboard_disk_held: {size} more held by running containers, freed on restart
dashboard_disk_modalBody: These images can be removed to free about {size}:
dashboard_disk_modalDeepNote: This deep clean also removes dangling untagged images left by other podman workloads on this machine. It never touches named data volumes.
system_php_ext_modulesHelp: Reported by php -m inside the PHP {version} image.
system_php_ext_notBuilt: PHP {version} has no image yet. Run 'servlo php:rebuild {version}' to build it.
system_php_ext_needsRebuild: This image predates your extensions and packages. Run 'servlo php:rebuild {version}' to bring it up to date.
system_php_ext_cannot: did not build on PHP {version}; a rebuild will not change that
system_php_ext_none: You have not added any custom extensions or packages.
system_php_ext_manageHelp: Manage these with servlo php:ext and servlo php:pkg. They apply to every PHP version.
databases_startHint: Start the engine to view its databases.
databases_loadFailed: Could not read the engine's databases.
databases_dropBody: This permanently deletes the database and all of its data, and cannot be undone.
databases_targetLabel: Which database these controls act on
databases_importedWithErrors: Imported {file}, but the engine reported {count} errors
databases_restoredWithErrors: Restored {name}, but the engine reported {count} errors
databases_importIssuesBody: The dump loaded, but the engine rejected these statements.
databases_importIssuesMore: and {count} more distinct errors not shown
databases_importFreshHint: The dump replaces what is there instead of loading on top of it. Statements that collide with existing tables are the usual reason an import ends on errors.
databases_importIssuesSkipped: servlo left these out on the way in, because they name roles or users this engine does not have:
entities_startHint: Start the service to browse its contents.
entities_loadFailed: Could not read what this service holds.
notify_center_empty: Nothing yet. Finished operations, failures and service updates land here.
system_remote_descriptionNoDns: DNS is disabled, so the dashboard is the only thing remote devices can use servlo for. Enable to set HTTP Basic credentials and bind the dashboard at {addr}. Sites need per-site {cmd} to be reachable.
system_dns_disabledHint: servlo-dns is disabled. Sites resolve through the system resolver via {tld} (RFC 6761). HTTPS is unavailable in this mode. To re-enable, set {setting} in {file} and run {cmd}.
shareDomain_title: Serve this site on your own domain?
shareDomain_body: Cloudflare Tunnel can serve the site on a domain you own, so the public address stays the same every time. Leave it empty for a throwaway trycloudflare.com URL.
shareDomain_previewEmpty: Its DNS has to be managed by Cloudflare.
shareDomain_rememberHint: Share straight away next time, without asking.
addsite_domainHint: The full domain this site is served on. Point its DNS at this server, then use Get SSL.
addsite_willCreate: This directory does not exist yet and will be created.
addsite_noFramework: No framework detected; the document root will be guessed.
addsite_deployKeyHint: Servlo clones with a deploy key of its own. Add the key below to the repository's deploy keys, then test the connection.
addsite_domainFirst: Enter the domain first: the deploy key belongs to the site.
addsite_archiveHint: A .zip of the project. If everything sits inside one folder, that folder is unwrapped.
sites_phpSettings_desc: These apply to this site alone. Each field writes every directive the setting needs, in PHP and in nginx, so raising one limit is never half done.
sites_phpSettings_executionHint: Writes max_execution_time and the nginx fastcgi read and send timeouts.
sites_phpSettings_loadFailed: Could not load this site's PHP settings.
sites_nginxSettings_desc: Response headers and static-asset caching for this site. Every save runs nginx -t before it counts, and keeps a backup of the config it replaced.
sites_nginxSettings_cacheHint: How long a browser may keep this site's CSS, JS, images and fonts. Never applies to PHP or HTML.
sites_nginxSettings_headersHint: Added to every response, including error pages. Servlo writes Strict-Transport-Security itself.
sites_nginxSettings_rawHint: For what the fields above do not cover. Included at the end of this site's server block, and never overwritten by servlo.
sites_nginxSettings_canonicalHint: One address for the site. The other is permanently redirected to it, so visitors and search engines see a single name.
sites_nginxSettings_canonicalUnavailable: Available once the site serves a domain and its own www form. Add the other one under Domains.
sites_redirects_desc: Send visitors somewhere else. A permanent redirect is cached by browsers, so leave it temporary unless the move is final.
sites_redirects_wholeHint: Everything on this site goes there, keeping the path and query. Leave empty to serve the site normally.
sites_redirects_rulesHint: Matched exactly, so /old does not also capture /older or anything under it.
sites_deploy_desc: Pulls the repository, puts back anything the update removed that this site protects, runs the deploy script, and reloads PHP so the new code is live. If the script fails, PHP is not reloaded and visitors stay on the last version that worked.
sites_deploy_pulledNotLive: The pull had already reached {commit}, so that code is on disk but was never made live.
sites_deployScript_desc: Runs after the pull, as the servlo user, with the site as its working directory. It stops at the first command that fails.
sites_deployScript_template: Not saved yet. This is the framework's template, and it lands at {path} when you save it.
sites_deployScript_migrates: This script runs a migration, so every deploy backs the database up first.
sites_deployScript_noMigration: No migration in this script, so no database backup is taken before a deploy.
sites_deployScript_loadFailed: Could not load this site's deploy script.
sites_deployExclude_title: Paths a deploy must not remove
sites_deployExclude_desc: When the repository tracks a directory the application writes to, a commit that removes it upstream removes it here too. These paths are put back after every pull.
sites_deployExclude_hint: One path per line, relative to the site directory.
sites_deployExclude_emptyWarning: Nothing is protected. A deploy will remove whatever the repository removed.
sites_deployExclude_reset: Go back to the framework's list ({paths})
sites_deployExclude_loadFailed: Could not load this site's exclude list.
sites_redeploy_desc: Checks the site out at {commit}, the commit it was running before the last deploy, and runs the deploy script again.
sites_redeploy_migrationWarning: Code only. Database migrations are not undone, so the schema stays as the last deploy left it and the older code has to run against it. To put the data back too, restore that deploy's snapshot yourself.
sites_redeploy_none: This site has no recorded deploy to go back from. The first deploy from this panel records where it started, and after that you can come back here.
sites_deployHistory_empty: Nothing deployed from this panel yet.
sites_deployHistory_loadFailed: Could not load this site's deploy history.
sites_webhook_desc: Give your git host this URL and it deploys the site every time somebody pushes. Off until you turn it on.
sites_webhook_branchHint: Only a push to this branch deploys. Leave it empty to deploy every branch, which is rarely what you want on a production site.
sites_webhook_urlHint: Paste this into your repository's webhook settings, content type application/json.
sites_webhook_secretOnce: Copy this now. It is shown once and never again; if you lose it, generate a new one.
sites_webhook_secretHidden: Set. Servlo does not show it again.
sites_webhook_regenerateHint: The URL stays the same and every old signature stops working.
sites_webhook_off: This site does not deploy on push.
sites_webhook_loadFailed: Could not load this site's webhook.
dbconn_trustedNote: Add that address to the database's trusted sources, or nothing here can reach it. On DigitalOcean: Databases, your cluster, Settings, Trusted sources.
dbconn_trustedUnknown: Servlo could not work out this server's public address ({error}), which is what a managed database's trusted sources need.
sites_cron_desc: Each entry is a systemd timer running its command inside this site's container. The last run and its output are read back from the journal, so they survive a restart of the panel.
sites_cron_empty: Nothing is scheduled on this site yet.
sites_cron_commandHint: Runs in the site's container, from the site's directory.
sites_cron_scheduleHint: Cron, or a systemd calendar. Any of these work:
sites_cron_captureHint: Off discards it, for a command that prints something every minute.
sites_cron_disabled: Keep the entry but stop running it
sites_cron_noCapture: This entry does not keep its output.
sites_cron_managedHint: Installed with the framework switch above, and changed there rather than here.
sites_cron_deleteBody: The timer and its unit are removed from this server and the command stops running. The site itself is untouched.
sites_cron_loadFailed: Could not load this site's schedule.
sites_cron_pseudoDetail: Servlo switches {label} off by setting {constant} in {file}, and runs this on a system timer instead:
files_liveWarning: This is the live site. Every change here takes effect immediately, with no undo and no backup.
files_binary: This is a binary file. Servlo will not open it in the editor.
files_fileTruncated: Only the first part of this file is shown, so it cannot be saved from here.
files_deleteBody: This removes {name} from the live site straight away. There is no undo and no backup.
files_deleteFolderBody: This removes {name} and everything inside it from the live site straight away. There is no undo and no backup.
files_permissionsIntro: Servlo sets these four modes and nothing else. Anything no rule claims is left as it is.
files_reason_directories: nginx and PHP-FPM have to traverse the tree to serve anything under it
files_reason_files: readable by the server, writable only by the account that owns the site
files_reason_executables: a file that is already executable stays executable, so artisan and vendor/bin keep working
files_reason_secrets: credentials and private keys stay readable only by the account that owns the site
files_permissionsNoChange: Nothing to change: every path already has the mode servlo would set.
files_permissionsSkipped: {count} path(s) skipped: symlinks, sockets and everything under .git.
files_permissionsPartial: This site is larger than servlo walks in one pass, so this plan covers part of it.
files_loadFailed: That folder could not be read.
smtp_usernameHint: Leave blank for a relay that authenticates by IP.
smtp_passwordHint: Stored on this server only, never shown again.
smtp_passwordKept: Leave blank to keep the current one
smtp_passwordKeptHint: A password is stored. Leave this blank to keep it.
smtp_fromAddressHint: Most providers only accept an address they have verified.
smtp_removeBody: The password is forgotten. Whatever was already written into the env file stays there until it is changed.
smtp_site_desc: Servlo runs no mail server. This is the SMTP account this site sends its own mail through.
smtp_panel_intro: The SMTP account Servlo sends its own alerts through, separate from any site's. Without it, alerts stay in the panel and the audit log.
smtp_panel_alertsTo: Alerts go to the sender address below, so point it at the inbox you actually read.
sftp_intro: Servlo authorises a key for one site and opens the session in that site's directory. Confining the session so it cannot leave needs root, and servlo prints that step rather than running it.
sftp_sameUser: Every site on this server runs as the same Linux account ({user}). SFTP confinement is a directory lock, not a boundary between people.
sftp_notConfined: sshd is not confining these sessions yet, so an authorised key reaches every site on this server.
sftp_confined: sshd is chrooting each session to its own site.
sftp_drifted: The installed sshd block is out of date, so a site added since is not confined.
sftp_labelHint: Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores.
sftp_publicKeyHint: Paste one line from a .pub file. Never a private key.
sftp_noKeys: No site has an SFTP key yet.
sftp_withdrawBody: The key stops working as soon as this is saved. Nothing else about the site changes.
sftp_setupIntro: Servlo is not root and will not run these. Servlo has written the sshd file to {path}; read it, then run the block yourself.
sftp_siteMissing: This site is no longer registered with servlo, but the key is still authorised.
backups_desc: Files and database, in one encrypted archive. Only this server's backup key opens it.
backups_checkOn: Test restore {schedule}. It restores into a database of its own and drops that again.
backups_noCheck: No scheduled test restore. A backup nothing has ever restored is not known to work.
backups_whenHint: Cron, an @shorthand, or a systemd calendar. Any of these work: daily · 30 3 * * * · *-*-* 03:30:00
backups_verifyWeekly: Test restore the newest backup every week
backups_verifyWeeklyHint: Restores it into a database of its own and drops that again. Your data is never touched.
backups_noneYet: None yet. Take one now, or add a schedule.
backups_keyNote: These can only be opened with {path}. Keep a copy of it somewhere else.
backups_verified: It restores: {n} tables came back, and the scratch database was dropped.
